comparison: Both evaluate software implementation and capabilities (C38-C39, C49, C77-C80, C86-C90). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of GPU acceleration and performance metrics. Peer reviewers unanimously praise the software as 'extremely well executed' with good documentation and availability. Both find the software development SUPPORTED, though peer review also includes model components (C5-C6, C33-C34, C44-C47) and software comparisons (C137-C140) that OpenEval addresses separately.

OpenEval R4 addresses model components and resolution (C5-C6, C33-C34, C44-C45, C50-C54) finding them SUPPORTED by Figure 1 and Methods. Peer R1 includes these model description claims alongside software implementation claims, also finding them SUPPORTED. Both agree on the technical achievements, with peer reviewers noting 'a lot of details provided.'

OpenEval R20 evaluates software comparisons (C137-C140) as SUPPORTED with fair and accurate descriptions. Peer R1 includes these claims in their overall positive software assessment. Both agree the comparisons are appropriate, with no challenges to how OpenNucleome is positioned relative to other tools.

Both evaluate validation against sequencing data (C40, C95-C106). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on high correlation coefficients (r=0.89) shown in Figures 4 and supplements. Peer reviewers affirm the model 'capture[s] many experimental observations accurately' and 'predict[s] several static quantities.' Both agree on strong quantitative validation, with peer review noting the iterative optimization approach.

Both evaluate MERFISH validation (C107-C111). OpenEval emphasizes this as true prediction since MERFISH data weren't used for training, finding correlation of 0.74 SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these results through overall positive assessment and explicit acknowledgment of 'time-dependent quantities' predictions. Both agree this represents successful independent validation.

OpenEval R12 evaluates telomere dynamics validation (C112-C113) as SUPPORTED based on Figure 5C-D showing subdiffusive behavior matching experiments. Peer R3 includes these dynamic validation results in their acceptance of 'time-dependent quantities like the mean-square displacement.' Both find the dynamic properties validation SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate single-cell heterogeneity findings (C41, C118-C121, C144). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on low correlation coefficients across trajectories and mechanistic explanations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall positive assessment and acknowledgment that model addresses 'dynamics of many nuclear components.' Both agree on heterogeneity findings without challenge.

OpenEval R13 evaluates arrested chromosome dynamics (C116-C117, C141-C143) as SUPPORTED by Figure 6A and consistency with theory/experiments. Peer R4 implicitly accepts these dynamics findings as part of overall model validation. Both find the predictions about limited chromosome movement SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R15 evaluates comparison of simulated vs experimental single-cell heterogeneity (C122-C123) as SUPPORTED by Figure 6 supplement 2A. Peer R4 implicitly accepts through overall validation acceptance. Both agree the model captures biologically relevant single-cell variation.

Both evaluate robust chromosome-speckle contacts (C42, C124-C126, C149-C151). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on high TSA-Seq correlation (r=0.72) and mechanistic explanation via nucleation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through positive reception of biological insights and mechanistic predictions. Both agree on selective robustness findings and coupled assembly mechanism.

Both evaluate nuclear zoning model and fixed points concept (C10-C13, C43, C146-C148). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on resilience of chromosome-nuclear body contacts across perturbations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through enthusiasm that work will 'attract significant interest' for biological insights. Both agree the nuclear zoning interpretation is reasonable.

Both evaluate nuclear deformation effects (C132-C136). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on Figure 7C showing differential effects on contacts vs TSA-Seq. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through statement that work 'significantly advances the field' and acknowledgment of perturbation capabilities. Both agree on these novel simulation findings.

OpenEval R7 evaluates nuclear deformation capability (C48, C129-C131, C166-C168) as SUPPORTED by Figure 7A-B and Methods description. Peer R6 includes deformation results in their acceptance of the model's ability to investigate 'steady-state organization and dynamics.' Both find the implementation SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R5 evaluates energy function design (C55-C69) as SUPPORTED with clear documentation and appropriate citations. Peer R7 raises UNCERTAINTY about model complexity, questioning parameter justification: 'The number of parameters in the energy function is very large. Any justification?' and 'the role of every parameter is not clear.' This represents a key disagreement—OpenEval finds the design well-justified while peer reviewers question parameter interpretability.

OpenEval R6 evaluates speckle model with phosphorylation dynamics (C46-C47, C63-C65, C75-C76, C162) as SUPPORTED and novel. Peer R7 includes these model components in their UNCERTAINTY about parameter complexity and justification. OpenEval sees clear documentation; peer reviewers want more clarity on parameter roles.

OpenEval R4 includes model components (C50-C54) finding them SUPPORTED. Peer R7 expresses UNCERTAINTY about the overall model parameterization including these components, stating 'One weakness of the model is that it has several parameters' and questioning their justification. Disagreement on whether model complexity is adequately justified.

Both evaluate parameter optimization workflow (C70-C74, C92-C93, C169-C172). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on Figure 2 and clear documentation of iterative procedure. Peer reviewers accept the methodology, noting model is 'built carefully' with iterative optimization, though they raise concerns about parameter interpretability elsewhere. Both agree the optimization approach is sound.

OpenEval R22 evaluates simulation protocols (C157, C160-C161, C173) as SUPPORTED with clear documentation. Peer R8 accepts simulation methodology, stating 'A lot of details are provided' and 'The success of the method is well illustrated.' Both find the technical implementation SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R6 includes semi-grand Monte Carlo method (C162) and speckle dynamics (C75-C76) as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 accepts the simulation methodology including these technical details. Both agree on the methodological soundness.
OpenEval R7 includes nuclear deformation implementation details (C166-C168) as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 accepts simulation methodology broadly. Both find the technical implementation adequate.

Both evaluate ensemble-level conservation despite heterogeneity (C152-C156). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on conserved average radial positions and contact preferences, with appropriate acknowledgment of uncertainty about origins. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall positive assessment. Both agree on these observations.

Both evaluate the interpretation about radial positioning heterogeneity (C145). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as reasonable interpretation with appropriate citations, though notes it's conceptual rather than directly tested. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through lack of criticism. Both agree this interpretation is reasonable given the data.

Both evaluate background claims about nuclear organization importance (C1-C3, C14-C18). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as well-established with appropriate literature citations. Peer reviewers accept these as 'standard background statements supported by extensive literature citations.' Both agree these foundational claims are uncontroversial.

Both evaluate background claims about experimental techniques (C19-C26). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as accurate descriptions with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept as established knowledge without question. Both agree these background claims are well-supported.
OpenEval R3 evaluates computational modeling background (C27-C29) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer R11 accepts these as standard background. Both agree on these foundational claims.

Both evaluate claims about gaps in the field (C30-C32). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as reasonable assessment motivating the work. Peer reviewers implicitly support this motivation through enthusiasm for OpenNucleome addressing the gap. Both agree the identified need is legitimate.

OpenEval R17 evaluates high-level capability claims (C10-C13) as part of fixed points concept. Peer R13 evaluates these as summary claims SUPPORTED by detailed results. Both agree these capability claims are demonstrated, though OpenEval focuses on mechanistic interpretation while peer review emphasizes overall achievement.

OpenEval R10 includes capability claim C7 about validation. Peer R13 includes this in high-level summary claims that are SUPPORTED by detailed validation results. Both agree the validation capabilities are demonstrated.

Both evaluate data sources and processing methods (C175-C180). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear documentation and appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accept these technical details without challenge, noting only minor documentation improvements needed. Both agree the data handling is adequate.

Both evaluate speculation about CPU scaling (C91). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting it's speculation not tested. Peer R15 accepts as part of technical description without challenge. Both recognize this as minor methodological observation, with OpenEval more explicitly flagging the speculative nature.
